summary:
Principado de Asturias stands under the national framework of Ley 4/2023, published in the Boletín Oficial del Estado on 28 February 2023, which applies uniformly across Spain's autonomous communities. The dedicated country assessment identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score this community separately, within a margin of 0.02.

Adults may rectify the registered sex entry through a simple administrative procedure directly before the Civil Registry, without prior surgical reassignment and without the former requirement of a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment; the right is grounded in the free development of personality under Article 10.1 of the Constitution. Article 43 sets the age of self-requested rectification at 16, with recognition possible from age 12 under conditions and consent rules for medical procedures on minors aged 12 to 16.

Access to sex-separated facilities rests on the gender marker recorded in the civil registry rather than on biological sex, so the administrative rectification is the operative basis for facility rules a visitor will encounter.

Transphobic motivation operates as an aggravating circumstance in sentencing under Article 22.4 of the Criminal Code, and Article 510 punishes hate speech with one to four years' imprisonment plus a fine of six to twelve months; both provisions derive from Organic Law 6/2022 rather than from Ley 4/2023. Gender expression appears in no article of the Criminal Code, so a hate crime based on gender expression has no free-standing offence, though discriminatory conduct and harassment on grounds of sexual orientation, sexual identity, gender expression and sexual characteristics are defined and sanctioned under Ley 4/2023.

Courts are applying the aggravation. A Tribunal de Instancia in Vigo used the transfobia aggravation for the first time, in a misdemeanour case over WhatsApp messages threatening a trans woman, and fined the author EUR 300. In Valencia, a juvenile gang that harassed, insulted, beat and filmed a trans person in a park to mock them produced a six-month prison sentence for the only adult defendant, while two minors were judged separately.

Same-sex marriage and full adoption rights have applied since 2005, and Spain is recognised in comparative rankings as among the most LGBT-friendly countries.
tangentialFactors:
With administrative self-declaration, Spain stands alongside Argentina, Ireland, Portugal and Uruguay in the small group of states offering registry-level gender recognition without a medical gate.

Ley 4/2023 also reformed the offences against sexual freedom at Articles 132, 173, 178 to 181 and 189 bis of the Criminal Code, so sexual-offence protections a visitor may rely on sit partly in the trans law itself and partly in the 2022 organic law on hate crime.

Human Rights Watch noted on 16 February 2023 that the provision allowing recognition from age 12 proved contentious during the congressional passage of the law; the political contestation concerned minors, not the adult administrative route a visitor would use.
localsOnly:
Residents of Principado de Asturias are entitled to discrimination data collection broken down by the causes covered by Ley 4/2023, and public measures must be adapted to rural circumstances within the community.

Discriminatory contract clauses are declared null and void, and the law combats LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing, while strengthening protections for unmarried same-sex couples.

Minors aged 12 to 16 are covered by specific consent rules for medical procedures, and recognition of the registered gender is possible from age 12 under conditions set by the statute.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory contains no Asturias-specific enforcement record: no hate-crime sentence, police complaint or Civil Registry decision from this community is sourced, so the two adjudicated examples cited here come from Vigo and Valencia and illustrate national practice rather than local practice.

Whether the Principado de Asturias has adopted regional implementing measures, a regional LGBTI equality plan or its own reporting under the data-collection duty is not sourced and remains unresolved.

The comparative ranking placing Spain among the most LGBT-friendly countries is referenced without the ranking body, year or methodology, so its precise basis is unresolved.
